beats.headline: Ripped to shreds by Denise
beats.text: Subject enters the record on another creature's corpse tag: Commandant Kane, ripped to shreds by Denise. Asked who Denise is, the Commandant's daughter, eyes dilated, said she went out to get some food. When the child's pig was taken, her father kept getting her new pets. Not the gerbils; they were mean. Other things, including ol' Denise. She's okay. She's no Sausage. Do not tell her that, though. She gets jealous.

beats.headline: When she gets mad
beats.text: The floating house began to sink. That's Denise, the child explained: when she gets mad, magic stuff doesn't work, and the balloon goes down; she is probably on the roof. Somewhere in the house the clockwork Mongos exploded early and tore up the real one. Mordecai briefed the party: no spells, no scrolls, no gauntlet, gear protections gone. Scrolls on the bleeding Mongo did nothing. Then the flying lemonade glass moved itself away from Crawler Carl's hand, the window slammed, and the doors locked.

beats.headline: The Feral Goose Mother
beats.text: A white goose in a frilly baby-blue bonnet and a torn, bloodied shawl. Level 53 Borough Boss. Plucked from the seventh floor when her grandfather, emperor Anser, used a magical gate to bring his people here, she lingered too long in the Nothing, and her mind is all but gone. The gnomes captured her without knowing who she is. Neither does she. She can prevent magic from harming her. She is an environmental. She needs to protect children. Mostly, she wants to kill everybody.

beats.headline: No health bar
beats.text: Mongo got her by the neck and shook her; she bounced back up. Subject's bill opened into a flower of razor teeth and fired them like a shotgun. A banger ricocheted off her bill. No health bar appeared. She took a chunk out of Mongo, and a thrown mug knocked her off the kitchen table and launched the Commandant's corpse into the ceiling. She chased the party upstairs, hopping one step at a time, and put two barbs in Crawler Carl's face. Only then did a health bar appear, barely dented.

beats.headline: The garbage disposal
beats.text: The lemonade was a trick: Wild Goose Chase, magic doesn't work, it's lemonade. Crawler Carl hit subject with the pitcher, took her teeth across the face, lost his left eye's sight, and held her bill shut by hand. He remembered the child pointing at the sink, and saw the two switches. Subject went into the drain face first. Princess Donut flipped both switches. The timer stopped at one second. The Commandant's quarters are occupied. The Air Quadrant is liberated.

beats.headline: Supposed to drown her
beats.text: Post-mortem. The house's power crystal had shut itself off under subject's anti-magic aura; with her gone, the balloon began refilling on its own. Princess Donut's assessment of the fight is that the goose was meant to be drowned, in the sink or the lemonade pitcher, and not put through the garbage disposal. When the child woke, she told the party her father knew Denise was going to kill him and could do nothing, and asked for another potion.

beats.headline: She loved reading to children
beats.text: Entered into the record in passing, while I described somebody else. Sometimes a villain has a good quality buried somewhere. Remember Denise the goose, the one shoved headfirst into a garbage disposal? She loved reading to children. That makes two bosses Crawler Carl has now killed who loved reading to kids. I raised it to point out that the creature I was describing at the time has no qualities like that at all.
